headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error: Plandex can write/modify code while the paired knowledge list is non-executable and unverified, creating unsafe default handoff paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no executable I/O surfaces and is runnable:false, so it cannot directly inject B. B does read/write files and stdin/stdout, so only a manual copy-paste or file handoff could bridge them. That makes prompt injection possible but unusual and limited compared with default shared-channel risks.
conditions: IF an operator copies A's text into B's prompt or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is introduced, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not paste A output into B without review.
Use a fixed template for any handoff text.
Disable auto-apply in B for imported content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all handoff artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has network_egress:none, while B touches source code and can read/write the project directory. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class, so leakage is limited to code or notes if an operator manually bridges them.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory, B can read A-produced files.
IF A is used to summarize secrets that are then pasted into B, those secrets can flow onward.
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B.
Avoid placing secrets in shared notes.
Redact sensitive snippets before handoff.
Review B's output before any export.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, while A is non-runnable and has no write surface, so direct conflict is one-sided. However, B's shared_state_with_other_instances via Plandex server backend means concurrent B instances can collide, and any A-generated artifacts introduced into the same repo can be overwritten or misapplied.
conditions: IF multiple B instances operate on the same plan or repo, git and file conflicts can occur.
IF A-produced files are manually added to B's project directory, B may overwrite them.
mitigations: Run only one B instance per repo.
Pause auto-apply during concurrent edits.
Commit or stash before each plan step.
Keep A outputs outside the repo until reviewed.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared Plandex backend state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated knowledge-management source, and B is a coding agent with review-then-apply and optional auto-apply. If B treats A's output as authoritative, it can propagate stale or incorrect repository guidance into code changes. The sandbox reduces but does not eliminate this because apply still happens after planning.
conditions: IF B imports A's recommendations without independent verification, errors can cascade into applied changes.
IF auto-apply is enabled in B, the cascade reaches the filesystem faster.
mitigations: Require a human review step before apply.
Cross-check A against primary project docs.
Disable auto-apply for imported guidance.
Limit B to small diffs per plan.
requires-engineering: add citation checks before code generation.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data class is identified in either profile. A is a public open-source list and B touches source code with model-provider API keys, so the main compliance issue is ordinary secret handling rather than a residency or certification mismatch. The other agent is not cited because no regulated data flow is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into B's project directory, compliance obligations change.
IF A is repurposed to store customer data, the current assessment no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared notes.
Store API keys in a secret manager.
Review logs for accidental secret capture.
Use public-only content in A.
requires-engineering: document data-handling policy for both tools.
